extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, media innovators, prospective Nieman Fellows, and readers interested in the future of journalism
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptive 'About' page for the Nieman Journalism Lab explaining its mission, audience participation, related Nieman Foundation programs, fellowship deadlines, and content-licensing terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage focus: highlight attempts at innovation and analyze success/failure
rubrics_metrics.description: "We want to highlight attempts at innovation and figure out what makes them succeed or fail.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Lab explicitly states it seeks to surface experiments and innovations in journalism and to analyze factors behind their success or failure so others can learn from them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: help journalism survive and thrive in the Internet age
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Nieman Journalism Lab is an attempt to help journalism figure out its future in an Internet age."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site’s overarching criterion for work and coverage is relevance to how quality journalism can survive and thrive in the online environment; items of interest should speak to that transition and its challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for practitioners: help reporters and editors adjust to online labor
rubrics_metrics.description: "We want to help reporters and editors adjust to their online labors; we want to help traditional news organizations find a way to survive; we want to help the new crop of startups that will complement — or supplant — them.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content and projects the Lab highlights should offer practical value for journalists and organizations adapting to digital workflows, business models, or audience engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader contributions: collaborative exchange and solicitation of tips
rubrics_metrics.description: "Primary among them are our readers; we hope your contributions will make the Lab a collaborative exchange of ideas. Tell us what’s happening around you, or what should be.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Lab solicits input from its readership; accepted contributions are expected to further collaborative discussion about the future of news and point to real developments or needs in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nieman Fellowships: application deadlines (procedural requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The annual deadline to apply for a fellowship is December 15 for international journalists and January 31 for Americans.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit procedural rule for fellowship applicants; prospective applicants must meet the stated annual deadlines for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nieman Reports editorial mission: critical examination of journalism practice
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Nieman Foundation also publishes the quarterly magazine Nieman Reports, the nation’s oldest magazine devoted to a critical examination of the practice of journalism.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial standard: content under the Nieman Reports umbrella focuses on critical, reflective examination of journalistic practice rather than promotional or purely news reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nieman Watchdog Journalism Project: encourage monitoring and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: "...the Nieman Watchdog Journalism Project, which encourages reporters and editors to monitor and hold accountable those who exert power in all aspects of public life.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a stated programmatic goal, projects and coverage associated with the Watchdog initiative should aim to reveal power dynamics and provide public accountability reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content licensing: Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial 3.0 United States License
rubrics_metrics.description: "Also unless otherwise noted, all content on this site is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial 3.0 United States License.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted uses: noncommercial translation, transformation, reprinting, or reuse provided the Lab and/or the work’s author are attributed, preferably with a link back. Examples given: translating the site, redistributing posts to students, reusing the Twitter feed text. For commercial or other uses, contact the Lab.
